correctness.rationale: Over C, -K is nef and big for the specified almost-general-position blow-up. Adjunction forces each irreducible negative curve to be smooth rational with self-intersection -1 or -2; Cauchy bounds its planar degree by 2. This exhausts 6 exceptional, 12 line and 3 conic (-1) curves plus the single (-2) triple-line strict transform. Two (-1) curves meeting once cannot jointly support a negative-definite matrix; for an independent set T, Schur complement of the added (-2) class is -2+r(T), hence only r<=1 is admissible. Bauer--Funke--Neumann Proposition 1.1 identifies these supports with Zariski chambers. The exact deletion recurrence and independently enumerated 2^21 subsets both return coefficients (1,22,156,490,725,447,57), total 1898; a separate 27-curve computation gives smooth baseline 2764. Integer arithmetic and finite enumeration verify finite combinatorics, while the written geometric argument proves no curves/supports were omitted.

originality.rationale: The classical correspondence between chambers and negative-definite supports is from Bauer--Funke--Neumann; it is not claimed new. Their tabulated 2764 count assumes six points in general position, where there are 27 (-1) curves, and therefore does not imply the special configuration with 21 (-1) curves plus a (-2) curve. Bauer--Schmitz treats improved enumeration and the Segre--Schur quartic, not the nodal cubic profile. Lubbes tabulates root configurations of weak del Pezzo surfaces, but not the Zariski support polynomial or chamber number. No equivalent count was identified in the inspected publications or targeted searches by exact value and equivalent geometric descriptions. The contribution is the explicit complete profile 1,22,156,490,725,447,57 (total 1898), with proof that it covers every negative curve and every chamber. Historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Specialized enumerative tables or nonindexed earlier computations may contain the same A1 chamber profile; database silence is not a uniqueness proof.

value.rationale: Zariski chambers govern stable base loci and piecewise-polynomial volumes, and the first A1 boundary of cubic surfaces is a canonical geometric degeneration, not an arbitrary family. Determining the entire seven-term negative-support polynomial provides a meaningful natural invariant and quantifies the decrease in chamber complexity by 866 compared with the smooth cubic while preserving maximal support six. The separation into 21-curve disjoint supports and extra-root supports reveals precisely how the exceptional (-2) curve changes the combinatorics. The result is mathematically motivated even though it uses established chamber correspondence and exact finite enumeration.
